entradas.text: I was in my office reading reports from the ministries about the current situation of the protests.
My next scheduled meeting was with Nia and Lileas, to discuss the law enforcement budget. I heard some knocks on the door.
Nia entered and took a seat in front of my desk. Lileas was absent.
“Good afternoon, Mr. President.”
“Lileas will be late. Apparently there was an urgent matter at the Ministry of the Interior she had to attend to. Shouldn't take long.”
“Very well. Let's wait.”
entradas.menu: “Very well. Let's wait.”

entradas.text: “What urgent matter?”
entradas.menu: “What urgent matter?”

entradas.text: “While we wait, why don't we have a little chat?”
“That's a couple of minutes less of Lileas. Great.”
entradas.menu: “That's a couple of minutes less of Lileas. Great.”

entradas.text: “She said something about supply distribution for the police forces. Nothing major.”
“You wouldn't find many who think otherwise.”
She laughed.
I returned to my reports and Nia smoothed back an errant strand of her hair. There was an awkward silence.
“This might come off as a little strange, but I am proud of you.”
“Despite everything, you are actually trying to reform the country.”
“It's *we* Nia, not *me*. I couldn't do any of this by myself. So no, I am proud of you.”
entradas.menu: “It's *we* Nia, not *me*. I couldn't do any of this by myself. So no, I am proud of you.”

entradas.text: “Flattery won't work on me. What do you want?”
entradas.menu: “Flattery won't work on me. What do you want?”

entradas.text: “This is just the beginning. There is so much more to do.”
entradas.menu: “This is just the beginning. There is so much more to do.”

entradas.text: “Well, thank you.”
“You certainly have a way with words, don't you?”
“Yes. Although there is a lot to do, the future looks promising. Thank you for that.”
“I wouldn't be the President otherwise.”
entradas.menu: “I wouldn't be the President otherwise.”

entradas.text: “Fair enough.”
She laughed.
“Words are just words. Actions are what's important.”
entradas.menu: “Words are just words. Actions are what's important.”

entradas.text: “And you seem to be doing well at both so far. Pros are cancelling out the cons for sure.”
“How are you really holding up, Anton? Being the President, I mean.”
She leaned forward.
“You are giving me hope that this country can get better.”
“It's not a matter of it *can* or it *can't*. It *will* get better. We will make it so.”
entradas.menu: “It's not a matter of it *can* or it *can't*. It *will* get better. We will make it so.”

entradas.text: “Your support gives me hope as well.”
entradas.menu: “Your support gives me hope as well.”

entradas.text: “We are all in this together after all.”
“I will follow you anywhere, as long as you keep making good decisions for the country.”
“For now, I just want to chat.”
“It's the hardest thing I have ever done in my life but it is also the best thing I have ever done in my life.”
entradas.menu: “It's the hardest thing I have ever done in my life but it is also the best thing I have ever done in my life.”

entradas.text: “Nothing I can't handle.”
entradas.menu: “Nothing I can't handle.”

entradas.text: “It feels like the whole weight of the country crushes me down every single day.”
entradas.menu: “It feels like the whole weight of the country crushes me down every single day.”

entradas.text: “Very well. I will take your word on that.”
“I can imagine. So much responsibility and so much power at the same time.”
“Everyone wants to be a president until they are one I guess.”
“I want to assist you and the country as best as I can. And to do that I have an idea. We need to eliminate the worst problem we have.”
“Corruption.”
“Nonsense. Our government is not a corrupt government.”
entradas.menu: “Nonsense. Our government is not a corrupt government.”

entradas.text: “And how do we do that?”
entradas.menu: “And how do we do that?”

entradas.text: “So finally you come to the point. What do you really want?”
entradas.menu: “So finally you come to the point. What do you really want?”

entradas.text: “Our government may not be, but think about the Supreme Court. Every single one of those Old Guards needs to answer to the law.”
“And it's not just the Old Guards. Think about the oligarchs. Everyone knows they have connections in the government. Who knows how deep the rabbit hole goes?”
“Please. Can't I hold a normal conversation with my president?”
“As the Minister of Justice, as you can guess, I have a passion for justice.”
“It's high time Old Guards and the Supreme Court stop holding the country in the palm of their hands.”
“That's why I want to form a new unit. The Anti-Corruption Police. That is my idea.”
“Give me time to think about it.”
entradas.menu: “Give me time to think about it.”

entradas.text: “That sounds like an excellent idea.”
entradas.menu: “That sounds like an excellent idea.”

entradas.text: “So? What if the anti-corruption police gets corrupted? What then?”
entradas.menu: “So? What if the anti-corruption police gets corrupted? What then?”

entradas.text: “I'm still figuring out the details myself right now, but of course there would be safety mechanisms in place.”
“I'm still figuring out the details myself right now, but think about the possibilities.”
“I'm glad you agree. I'm still figuring out the details myself right now, but think about the possibilities.”
“I want to assist you and the country as best as I can. Unfortunately, my hands are tied with the current budget allocation we have for the law enforceme--”
“Also, one more thing.”
“About Lileas.”
“I wouldn't trust her if I were--”
“I hope that I'm not interrupting your conversation.”
She barely finished the sentence before we heard a knock on the door. Nia almost jumped in her chair. Lileas Graf entered the room.
“A chat about your emergency decree.”
“A chat about the so called *reform* package.”
“What of it?”
entradas.menu: “What of it?”

entradas.text: “Sure, let's have a chat.”
entradas.menu: “Sure, let's have a chat.”

entradas.text: “I had my reasons.”
entradas.menu: “I had my reasons.”

entradas.text: “No need to go on defensive. But I will say this.”
“Nothing. Apart from the fact that we are repeating Soll's mistakes again.”
“Or the fact that this is not what we were elected for.”
“Or the fact that...You get my point.”
“You don't agree with my decision.”
entradas.menu: “You don't agree with my decision.”

entradas.text: “Was I not clear enough?”
“Times change. Internal and external threats have to be eliminated.”
entradas.menu: “Times change. Internal and external threats have to be eliminated.”

entradas.text: “You are repeating Soll's mistakes again.”
“This is not what we were elected for.”
“Soll's mistakes? He made this great country what it currently is.”
entradas.menu: “Soll's mistakes? He made this great country what it currently is.”

entradas.text: “A place where there are innocent people getting murdered on the streets because of internal conflicts. Is this your understanding of a great country?”
“Times do change but the methods clearly not.”
She sighed.
“I keep thinking about it and I come to the same conclusion every time. There is no way I can get behind this. Don't forget that I have a vote in the Court.”
“Trust me. I am doing all of this for the well being of Sordland.”
entradas.menu: “Trust me. I am doing all of this for the well being of Sordland.”

entradas.text: “Enough. I already made my decision and what is left is for you to follow it.”
entradas.menu: “Enough. I already made my decision and what is left is for you to follow it.”

entradas.text: She opened her mouth to answer but there was knock at the door. Lileas Graf entered the room.
“Mr. President. Nia.”
“No, not at all. We were just discussing...a few things.”
Nia smiled at Lileas.
“Well then... Let's go straight in.”
“Go ahead.”
entradas.menu: “Go ahead.”

entradas.text: “We will provide a brief update on the situation of law enforcement.”
“The Ministry of Justice and the Supreme Court is working in close collaboration with the Ministry of Interior to address the protests in the country.”
“I must add that thanks to the hard work of our judiciary, the law enforcement forces assigned to my ministry are doing their jobs efficiently.”
“Nia?”
I nodded.
entradas.menu: Nod.

entradas.text: Lileas took the seat next to Nia as she continued talking.
“Our efforts ramped up quite a bit recently. Especially after the declaration of the emergency decree.”
“I would call it the success of our forces on the ground, not due to the judicial branch of our government.”
Lileas shot Nia a brief withering glance.
“As expected, after the budget reduction, the morale of the employees are at an all time low. Many of them face the risk of losing their jobs now.”

“Agreed. The Ministry of Justice was hit the worst. The backlog of the court cases are so high that the judges do not even have time to look at smaller cases, postponing these to months or years later.”

“This comes at an even bigger surprise considering one of the promises that you have made was to focus on our security forces. Yet here we are, thinking about how to fire our security force personnel during mass protests.”
“This is ridiculous!”
“Yet here we are, with mass protests happening in the country, talking about how we have to fire our security force personnel.”
“This causes a disastrous bottleneck. How can we deal justice if we can't even find time for these cases?”
“As expected, the budget increase has boosted morale of the employees in the law enforcement agencies. In these dire times, my people and Nia's people are especially delighted.”
“Agreed. At the Ministry of Justice, we are very happy with the decision as well. The backlog of the court cases are dwindling and we have started to fulfil the needs of the current situation.”
“And for that, all I will say is... Bravo! This was an excellent decision.”
“I think you will be glad to hear that the support for you among the forces is at an all time high, Mr. President.”
“This came as a pleasant surprise to many in the Ministry of the Interior since it was not even one of our campaign promises.”
“Certainly a step in the right direction.”
“The current budget has dampened hopes of more funding in the force.”
“Agreed. Many in the Ministry of Justice hoped for an increase and were not satisfied with the decision.”
“The decisions made needs to reflect the current situation of the country. This was certainly not the right decision when we are dealing with mass protests.”
“This comes at an even bigger surprise considering one of the promises that you have made was to focus on our security forces. Yet here we are, exactly where we started at.”
“Yet here we are, with mass protests happening in the country. We are standing exactly where we were before.”
“Regardless, this means we will have to deal with the growing court backlog. It is manageable but it will be a challenge for sure.”
“Thank you. I am glad you approve.”
entradas.menu: “Thank you. I am glad you approve.”

entradas.text: “I did what was expected from me. That's all.”
entradas.menu: “I did what was expected from me. That's all.”

entradas.text: “Of course it was the right decision. I made it, after all.”
entradas.menu: “Of course it was the right decision. I made it after all.”

entradas.text: “Of course.”
Nia cast a sidelong look at Lileas.
Nia nodded.
“Of course.”
“Of course.”
“Don't worry. I am sure you will manage.”
entradas.menu: “Don't worry. I am sure you will manage.”

entradas.text: “I had to make sacrifices for the good of Sordland.”
entradas.menu: “I had to make sacrifices for the good of Sordland.”

entradas.text: “You will do as you are told with what you have.”
entradas.menu: “You will do as you are told with what you have.”

entradas.text: “These sacrifices might've very well damaged the structural integrity of Sordland.”
“That remains to be seen but the ripples are already being felt across the country. I hope this decision is not the beginning of something bad.”
“Tell that to the policemen on the ground when they are overwhelmed by the protestors.”
“The ripples are already being felt across the country. I hope this decision is not the beginning of something bad.”
Lileas and Nia looked at each other and fell silent.
“Don't worry. I am sure you will manage.”
entradas.menu: “Don't worry. I am sure you will manage.”

entradas.text: “I had to make sacrifices for the good of Sordland.”
entradas.menu: “I had to make sacrifices for the good of Sordland.”

entradas.text: “These sacrifices might've very well damaged the structural integrity of Sordland.”
“Tell that to the policemen on the ground when they are overwhelmed by the protestors.”
“That remains to be seen but the ripples are already being felt across the country. I hope this decision is not the beginning of something bad.”
“You will do as you are told with what you have.”
entradas.menu: “You will do as you are told with what you have.”

entradas.text: “The ripples are already being felt across the country. I hope this decision is not the beginning of something bad.”
Lileas and Nia looked at each other and fell silent.
“Well then. Let's move on to what we are actually here for.”
“Due to the budget increase, we can start doing much more as the main branches of security in Sordland.”
“However...”
“Why should I pick Ministry of Interior?”
entradas.menu: “Why should I pick Ministry of Interior?”

entradas.text: “Why should I pick Ministry of Justice?”
entradas.menu: “Why should I pick Ministry of Justice?”

entradas.text: “The Ministry of Interior is a much more significant and important government agency that is in need of the funds. Especially during these times where there are many protests in the country.”
“This seems to be an organizational issue, not a funding one. The Interior needs the money more for the police and local governments.”
“What if I decide to balance the budget between Ministry of Interior and Ministry of Justice?”
entradas.menu: “What if I decide to balance the budget in between Ministry of Interior and Ministry of Justice?”

entradas.text: “Balancing the budget won't help as much. The current situation clearly demands that a decisive choice be made to benefit the nation. ”
“Exactly. When deciding you must look at the bigger picture. I believe you will make the right choice and pick the Ministry of Interior.”
“I agree. We need to focus on one ministry to achieve tangible results.”
“A decision has to be made about the budget balance between the Ministry of Interior and the Ministry of Justice.”
“Good luck prosecuting criminals or going through local government laws without enough judges, Lileas.”
“Each day the stacks of legal cases are piling up for judges. Cases for corruption and criminals are delayed due to a lack of funds.
“Of course what would make the most sense in the current situation would be to support the much neglected Ministry of Justice that would improve the legal system in Sordland.”
“I have already made my decision.”
entradas.menu: “I have already made my decision.”

entradas.text: “I am ready to make a decision.”
entradas.menu: “I am ready to make a decision.”

entradas.text: Lileas and Nia leaned forward.
“The funds will go the Ministry of Justice to reduce the court backlog and improve the justice system.”
entradas.menu: “The funds will go the Ministry of Justice to reduce the court backlog and improve the justice system.”

entradas.text: “The budget will be distributed equally in between the Ministry of Interior and Ministry of Justice.”
entradas.menu: “The budget will be distributed equally in between the Ministry of Interior and Ministry of Justice.”

entradas.text: “The funds will go to the Ministry of Interior to be used to improve the police and local governments.”
entradas.menu: “The funds will go to the Ministry of Interior to be used to improve the police and local governments.”

entradas.text: “Tell me, Nia. Who brings the criminals before the justices? Let me answer. The police forces connected to Ministry of Interior.”
“Due to the budget decrease, we have no choice but to cut funding from a branch.”
“However...”
“Exactly. When deciding you must look at the bigger picture and I believe you will make the right choice.”
“You need to make a decision to determine which branch gets the cut.”
“Why should I cut funding from Ministry of Interior?”
entradas.menu: “Why should I cut funding from Ministry of Interior?”

entradas.text: “Why should I cut funding from Ministry of Justice?”
entradas.menu: “Why should I cut funding from Ministry of Justice?”

entradas.text: “What if I decide to cut funding equally from Ministry of Interior and Ministry of Justice?”
entradas.menu: “What if I decide to cut funding equally from Ministry of Interior and Ministry of Justice?”

entradas.text: “The funds will be decreased from the Ministry of Justice. It is clearly the less important agency with the current situation.”
entradas.menu: “The funds will be decreased from the Ministry of Justice. It is clearly the less important agency with the current situation.”

entradas.text: “I am ready to make a decision.”
entradas.menu: “I am ready to make a decision.”

entradas.text: “The funds will be decreased from the Ministry of the Interior. We need to solve the court backlog issue to deal justice.”
entradas.menu: “The funds will be decreased from the Ministry of the Interior. We need to solve the court backlog issue to deal justice.”

entradas.text: Lileas and Nia leaned forward.
“I have already made my decision.”
entradas.menu: “I have already made my decision.”

entradas.text: “Budget will be cut equally from the Ministry of Interior and Ministry of Justice.”
entradas.menu: “Budget will be cut equally from the Ministry of Interior and Ministry of Justice.”

entradas.text: “Ministry of Interior and our police forces on the ground play a much larger and a more important role during these times where there is a threat to our internal safety.”
“Simple. It's because Ministry of Interior can't afford a reduction unless you want the whole country to be overrun with protestors.”
“The Ministry of Interior is one of the well funded government agencies in Sordland. The same can't be said about Ministry of Justice.”
“We need decisive action. Cutting funding from both branches won't help anyone.”
“Hah. And tell me Lileas, how are you going to bring the criminals to justice if our judges have to postpone court dates to 6 months, 1 year later.”
“That doesn't mean anything. The Ministry of Interior is far more critical in function. Especially now.”
“Tell me, Nia. Who brings the criminals before the justices? Let me answer. The police forces connected to Ministry of Interior.”
“Look at it this way. Ministry of Justice has never been well-funded in Sordland while the Ministry of Interior was always more lucky, already causing this uneven balance in between the two.”
“Our court cases have been piling up with no end in sight. We already have a bottleneck. If we worsen the situation, our whole justice system will fall.”
“It doesn't even matter who or how many criminals you catch with your forces if justice can't be dealt.”
“This is completely absurd and unbefitting for the President of Sordland.”
“I knew you would see reason. Thank you.”
“I knew that we would be on the same side, Mr. President.”
“This is ridiculous.”
“Bad decision making.”
“The right choice. It was time that Ministry of Justice got the funds it needs.”
“I was expecting you to be different, Mr. President.”
“Before you decide, I would like to remind you of your obligations and promises as the leader of this administration, Mr. President.”
“What will it be?”
“Before you decide, I would like to remind you of your obligations and promises as the leader of this administration, Mr. President.”
“What will it be?”
“Bad decision making.”
“I was expecting you to be different, Mr. President.”
“This is completely absurd and unbefitting for the President of Sordland.”
“This is ridiculous.”
A brief moment of deliberation passed. Lileas and Nia got up from their seats.
“I must return to the ministry to implement necessary changes.”
“Me too.”
They left the room.
As soon as the door closed, I could their muffled voices as they argued.
“Before we begin, I'd like to mention your call to boost the police has helped us tremendously in maintaining public safety.”
“A few incidents seemed to have happened due to the inexperience of the recruits coming from the police academy. They were relieved of duty immediately.”
A brief moment of deliberation passed. Nia got up from her seat.
A brief moment of deliberation passed. Lileas and Nia got up from their seats.
“Well then. I must now return to the ministry.”
They left the room.
“Me too.”
As soon as the door closed, I could hear their muffled voices as they argued.
A brief moment of deliberation passed. Lileas got up from her seat.
A brief moment of deliberation passed. Nia and Lileas leaned back in their seats.
“I must return to the ministry to implement the necessary changes.”
“Very well. See you soon, Nia. I need to have a few words with Mr. President.”
“I must return to the ministry to implement necessary changes.”
“Very well. See you soon, Lileas. I need to have a few words with Mr. President.”
Lileas left the room.
Nia smiled thinly and left the room. Lileas turned to me.
“That's why I am proposing the formation of a Secret State Police.”
“I have a proposal.”
“We have been battling with terror for a long time now. I want to put an end to it.”
“If you accept, this will give our administration power to handle the threats more...discreetly as well.”
“Very well. Form the Secret State Police.”
entradas.menu: “Very well. Form the Secret State Police.”

entradas.text: “I don't think so. Our current structure is enough.”
entradas.menu: “I don't think so. Our current structure is enough.”

entradas.text: “Excellent. I will start the prep work.”
“Unfortunate.”
“You are making one good decision after another today, Mr. President.”
“I will be in touch.”
“Regardless, this has been a very productive day. I have to take my leave now as well.”
Lileas got up and left the room.
“Here is my proposal.”
“Corruption has always been a major issue with any government. It is the root of all evil.”
“That's why I'm proposing the formation of the Anti-Corruption Police.”
“If you accept, this will give our administration the ability to deal with corruption quickly and decisively.”
“Very well. Form the Anti-Corruption Police.”
entradas.menu: “Very well. Form the Anti-Corruption Police.”

entradas.text: “I don't think so. Our current structure is enough.”
entradas.menu: “I don't think so. Our current structure is enough.”

entradas.text: “Excellent. I will start the prep work.”
“You are making good decisions after good decisions today, Mr. President.”
Nia got up and left the room.
“Unfortunate.”
“Regardless, this has been a very productive day. I have to take my leave now as well.”
“I will be in touch.”
Lileas and Nia got up and left the room.
“I don't think so. Our current structure is enough.”
entradas.menu: “I don't think so. Our current structure is enough.”

entradas.text: “That's why we are proposing the formation of a Community Police.”
“We have a proposal.”
“Unfortunate.”
“We have been battling with the unrest in the country for a long time now. We want to put an end to it.”
“Regardless, this has been a very productive day. I have to take my leave now as well.”
“We will be in touch.”
“Exactly. If you accept, this will give our administration power to handle the unrest swiftly.”
“You are making good decision after good decision today, Mr. President.”
“Excellent. We will start the prep work.”
“Very well. Form the Community Police.”
entradas.menu: “Very well. Form the Community Police.”

entradas.text: They looked at each other before turning to me.
“Thank you, Mr. President.”
“As a sub branch of Ministry of Justice, the ACP would be given full authority by the Presidency to investigate corrupt government officials and citizens.”
“The Community Police would be picked from trustworthy members of the local community. It will give us greater coverage over the country to combat criminals.”
“This would especially come in handy when dealing with corruption in higher positions. The Supreme Court and oligarchs that meddle in politics are just a few examples.”
“While some in the law enforcement agencies look at this negatively we do believe it has the potential to be successful.”
“This would be a new force that would be in charge of handling internal security and intelligence matters.”
“The primary aim of this program is to detect and prevent subversive elements before they take any harmful action against the state.”
“This will come in handy to deal with the protests.”
“I must thank you, Mr. President, for the support with the riot gear. The Police Forces definitely needed it.”
“I must say, Mr. President, that your lack of support to the law enforcement is taking its toll on the police forces. They are crumbling away... But we'll talk about that soon.”
“What makes things worse is that our request to fund the lacking riot control equipment has been ignored.”
“At least you have fulfilled our request to fund additional riot control equipment that will allow us to maintain order to some degree.”
“At least you have fulfilled our request to fund additional riot control equipment that will allow us to maintain order to some degree.”
“What makes things worse is that our request to fund the lacking riot control equipment has been ignored.”
“The situation is still not good.”
“A wise choice.”
“I am sorry for being late. There was an important matter at the ministry. The security forces of Bergia are arbitrarily not cooperating with my department and created some minor annoyances.”
“Luckily they didn't completely botch their tasks, and actually uncovered a large network of priests that are recruiting Bergians for the Bludish Freedom Front.”
"This sounds very significant. Do you want to explain more?"
"Good. Do your best to keep the miscommunication with the Governor's forces to a minimum. We need to take the war against terror seriously."
"You were late, Ms. Graf. But now that you are here, let's begin with the meeting."
"Of course."
"The issue was a miscommunication about an ongoing investigation inside Bergia. But as I said, it didn't affect the results in a negative way."
"The investigation itself, however, revealed some troubling facts. We suspect the existence of a massive network of BFF-aligned priests currently serving in Bergia."
"We have discovered that most of the existing Golcondist sanctuaries and communities inside Bergia are indeed working directly for the BFF."
"Several reports also point to a possible infiltration of the Dastnurist and Wruhecist communities by these Golcondist sects. May the Divine God forgive us if this is true."
"Thank you for the brief report, Lileas."
"This is worrying news. Keep following the lead. We cannot let these sects divide our society."
"Tell me about the Golcondists."
"If you want my honest opinion, they are a group of dangerous radicals who follow a warped interpretation of Wruhecist Nurity. Most faithful Nurists wouldn't want to have anything to do with them."
"I don't appreciate you speaking like that, Lileas. The majority of the Bludish community in Sordland practice Golcondism."
"Don't normalize it, Ms. Morgna. They are a plague on this earth. Even orthodox Wruhecists do not like them."
"As a devout Dastnurist myself, I haven't experienced any divide in Sordland between our religion and mainstream Wruhecism. Bless St. Dast -- all practitioners of Nurity live in peace here..."

"...Except the Golcondists, of course. Their extremist beliefs are an abomination. And unfortunately, after the Wruhecist Revolution in Derdia, now we also have a Golcondist state that uses the influence of their faith internationally."
"As a matter of fact, the Nurist Republic of Derdia is one of the BFF's suspected supporters. Their aims are clearly one and the same."
"Of course, Mr. President."
"Thank you for the explanation, Lileas."
"Do you suspect any other countries are supporting the BFF together with Derdia?"
"Keep following that lead. We cannot let countries like Derdia try and destabilize us with religion."
"Of course, Mr. President."
"I suspect the Kingdom of Rizia is involved in this along with Derdia. However, the biggest player is Rumburg and we have clear evidence of their interference. Our focus must be on them."
"I don't think we should damage our international relations over unproven suspicions. Our direct neighbors have much more influence over us."
"Besides, this isn't the topic of this meeting. I think it's best to discuss this in an external security meeting -- when or if -- enough proof is collected."
"You're right."
"I thought you'd be familiar with them as a Bergian yourself."
"I thought you might have encountered them during your university days."
"To be honest, I couldn't care less about religion."
"May the Divine God save your soul."
"If this is over, why don't we start the meeting?"
"Unfortunately, due to my limited authority in the Special Zone of Bergia, I cannot control their operations."
